title: Usage Economics Dashboard: pricing controls & export-first token attribution flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype an export-first Token Economics Dashboard within Redwood Console that surfaces per-request and aggregated token-level cost attribution, alongside interactive pricing controls/simulators for PMs and finance users. The feature should support ad-hoc CSV/Parquet exports for large date ranges, per-route and per-model breakdowns, and a lightweight pricing preview that lets teams estimate cost after changing batching/quantization/routing policies. Deliverables: Figma flows, high-fidelity desktop screens, small set of mobile adjustments, and handoff spec (tokens, visualizations, accessibility notes). Out of scope: backend aggregation pipelines and billing engine changes (ENG to own).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows a time-series of token spend and unit counts with selectable granularity (hour/day/week) and model/route filters
Per-route and per-model tables include columns for tokens_generated, tokens_consumed, effective_cost_per_token, and attributed_cost with sorting and column toggle
Export flow supports CSV and Parquet, with streaming download for large ranges and preview of estimated row count before export
Pricing simulator modal allows users to change pricing levers (batch size, quantization profile, routing tier) and see delta preview on selected date range
Design handoff includes component states, microcopy for export throttling/limits, and accessibility notes (contrast/keyboard/aria labels)
design_notes: Primary layout: left rail filters + main chart row + attribution table beneath + right rail pricing simulator
Chart prototypes include stacked area (cost by model) and line view (tokens vs cost) with hover tooltips showing sample request examples
Attribution row-level view: show example request id, route, model variant, input_length, output_length, cache_hit boolean, and deduced cost contribution
Export-first pattern: 'Preview export' step that runs a fast aggregate query, returns estimated rows and size, then allows streaming download to avoid timeouts
Pricing controls are lightweight and modal-first; support 'apply to selection' or 'run simulation without applying' actions
Use visual affordances for price-impact (green down / red up chips) and clear CTA to 'Create billing alert' from simulator results
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Pre-aggregate vs live rollups: decided to surface pre-aggregates for day-level queries and async previews for hour-level exports to keep UI snappy
Row-level sample vs full export: show sampled example rows inline (100 rows) to let users validate attribution before heavy exports

Pricing simulator fidelity: prototype provides approximate estimates using existing model of unit prices and assumed batching efficiency; exact cost requires backend recalculation so simulator should surface a certainty badge
Placement of pricing controls: chose modal from right rail to avoid pushing the core analytics grid off-screen for heavy tables
Export formats: include Parquet for analytics teams and CSV for quick shareability; parity with storage naming convention required by ENG
review_feedback: Sofia Martinez (PM): +1 on simulator but requested a 'compare against baseline' feature to show historical baseline and projected savings
Ravi Kapoor (Engineering): flagged streaming export implementation details; suggests adding rate-limit warnings and max-export-size guardrails in UI copy
Olivia Kim (Data): asked for a column that maps to billing invoice item keys to ease reconciliation with finance
DesignOps: noted accessibility issue with small chips for delta indicators; asked for larger hit targets and text alternatives
Security Reviewer (Jake Li): requested explicit note in export modal about PII and recommended tied policy to KMS-protected exports for enterprise customers
next_steps: Incorporate PM feedback: add 'compare to baseline' mockups and update simulator copy
Sync with ENG to define export API contract and streaming protocol; get back-end estimate from ENG-2101
Add a small mobile layout with collapsible rails for top requests and a vertical simulator flow
Finalize handoff bundle in Figma and export component spec to Storybook (Design -> Dev handoff)
Schedule review session with Finance to validate mapping to invoice items (invite Olivia Kim and Aaron Brooks)
